correctness.rationale: The known OU and CIR stationary age mixtures give explicit independent diagonal-difference and nonnegative offdiagonal densities. The exact polar gap-density identity reduces the small-gap law to integrable beta angular factors. Negative variance moments are finite precisely for beta<2; at beta=2 a logarithmic age singularity appears; for beta>2 gamma substitution yields the sharp coefficient r/[a(beta-2)]. Dominated convergence gives the three gap asymptotics. The common second moment follows by taking expectations of Delta²=(X-Y)²+4C². A standalone program evaluated 97 deterministic/numeric assertion groups, including exact mixture and angular quadrature, plus 1.75 million independent- and 1.75 million simultaneous-clock Monte Carlo 2x2 samples in aggregate across five indices. Unproved general-size limits are excluded.

originality.rationale: Akemann–Majumdar–Päßler provide all stationary entry marginals and the independent-entry product distribution (prior work), but explicitly leave independent-reset eigenvalue distributions analytically difficult and report larger-size numerical densities. Biroli–Majumdar–Schehr already prove the full simultaneous-reset two-body gap law and its beta=1 transition: this is acknowledged, not presented as novel. The claimed advance is a distinct independent-entry small-gap theorem with its beta=2 transition, logarithmic boundary, exact coefficients and moment-matching contrast. The singular stationary-age analysis is necessary; direct title searches are not treated as novelty proof.
residual_risks: A general published small-ball or random-matrix universality theorem may implicitly evaluate the independent-reset beta=2 exponent.
Existing exact stationary matrix-entry measures logically encode the spacing law; priority attaches to the nontrivial extracted asymptotic and interpretation, not a new matrix distribution.
Independent external priority assessment and independently rerun mathematical checks have not been performed.

value.rationale: Level repulsion is a central local diagnostic of random-matrix universality. The two reset strategies share all one-entry laws and exactly the same mean-square gap yet have a strict measurable difference in the near-degeneracy probability: the independent-clock repulsion exponent saturates at beta=2 rather than the known shared-clock beta=1. The exact phase boundary and logarithmic correction are structurally motivated, hold for a complete continuous parameter range, and reveal a non-obvious limit of low-order spectral observables, not an arbitrary finite table.
